stories.title: Fast-moving California wildfire burns homes as people are ordered to leave
summary: Fanned by the fierce Santa Ana winds, the Norte Fire is one of 13 burning across the state.

stories.title: NASA’s Roman Space Telescope exceeds expectations by nearly 30%
summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has exceeded expectations after engineers made incredibly tiny adjustments to sharpen its view of the universe.
By moving a mirror just one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, the team helped bring its powerful instruments into near-perfect alignment.
Roman’s Wide Field Instrument now produces image quality nearly 30% better than predicted, promising exceptionally sharp cosmic surveys.

stories.title: This bird flies thousands of miles, but its wings have a catch
summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected trade-off in the wings of the European nightjar, a bird that migrates thousands of kilometers but sacrifices high-speed flight efficiency to hunt insects with remarkable agility.
Even more surprisingly, it generates thrust on the upward wingbeat, a technique that could inspire new flying technologies.

stories.title: Brain cells meant to protect us may be fueling cognitive decline
summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising cause of age-related cognitive decline involving brain cells previously thought to be entirely beneficial.
As these cells become dysfunctional, they can produce abnormal amounts of myelin, disrupting nerve fibers and potentially contributing to worsening memory and thinking skills.

stories.title: NASA’s Webb reveals the wild weather of a mysterious world 20 light-years away
summary: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has revealed that a turbulent world 20 light-years away has a surprisingly orderly weather system, with three recurring atmospheric states driven by temperature changes and shifting clouds.
The breakthrough gives scientists a powerful new tool for uncovering weather patterns on distant worlds and understanding the conditions that shape their atmospheres.

stories.title: Scientists discover how deep sleep builds muscle, burns fat, and boosts the brain
summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising two-way relationship between sleep and growth hormone, revealing how the brain carefully balances physical recovery with wakefulness.
The findings could help explain why poor sleep harms metabolism and brain health, potentially opening the door to new treatments for sleep and neurological disorders.

stories.title: Avian flu and costs among reasons for loss of captive birds at Castle Espie
summary: Difficulties in transporting animals since Brexit has contributed to the decline in the number of captive birds.

stories.title: Why hasn't the UK had any named storms yet?
summary: So far this autumn wet and windy weather patterns have been steered away from the UK.

stories.title: Scientists predicted doomsday for November 13, 2026. Should we be worried?
summary: In 1960, scientists predicted that runaway population growth would bring humanity to the brink of destruction on November 13, 2026, and their mathematical forecasts remained surprisingly accurate for decades.
But as birth rates declined and population growth slowed, the terrifying prediction unraveled, revealing how even convincing scientific models can fail when human behavior changes.

stories.title: SpaceX just delivered some very strange cargo to the International Space Station
summary: SpaceX just delivered some surprisingly strange cargo to the International Space Station, including tiny brain models, 3D heart tissue, and technology for making artificial retinas in space.
Scientists hope these experiments could unlock new ways to treat devastating brain diseases, restore eyesight, and test future medicines.
The shipment also includes materials for creating unusual glass in near weightlessness and the station’s final upgraded solar arrays.

stories.title: James Webb reveals a strange bulge in an alien planet's atmosphere
summary: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope have discovered that a distant alien planet's atmosphere is surprisingly lopsided.
Located 1,300 light-years away, the scorching gas giant WASP-17b experiences powerful winds that redistribute heat, causing one side of its atmosphere to bulge outward.
A groundbreaking new mapping technique revealed these hidden distortions, confirming predictions about how extreme temperatures and winds shape alien worlds.

stories.title: US senators call for investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions
summary: Ukraine says temporary speed limits to the Starlink internet network disrupted its battlefield missions.
